thread:
Jordan: Heads up — seeing a spike in partial/fragmented responses on the live ingestion websocket around 10:45 UTC. No obvious error in the app logs. Anyone know the best dashboards/traces to check so I can correlate with infra alerts?
Irene: Start with the streaming grafana playlist: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/streaming/live-ingest-overview — panels for per-shard p50/p95 chunk times, reconnects, and partial-frame rate. Also check the 'ingest-ws' service in Jaeger for any tail latency hops.
Alex: Metric names that helped me before: `streaming.ws.chunk_duration.p95`, `streaming.ws.partial_frame.rate`, `streaming.ws.disconnects.count` and `ingest.kv_cache.hit_rate`. If you want raw logs filter `index=ingest-ws` and look for `partial_frame` or `send_error`.
Sam: FYI ops-alert fired at 10:46 — ops-bot posted a link below. Current alert threshold is partial_frame.rate > 0.05 for 2m. That's been noisy on congestion days. I'd lean to either 0.08 for 1m or keep 0.05 but require 3m.
Lee: Can you paste the exact trace id if you find one? I can pull the logs from the node that owned that shard and grep for websocket write timeouts.
Jordan: ops-bot link was in the channel: https://alerts.redwood.company/alert/ALRT-9876 — shows a 1.2x jump in p95 chunk time. I'll grab the trace id and post.
ops-bot: Alert ALRT-9876 triggered at 2026-03-15T10:46:11Z — rule: partial-frame-high — value: 0.067 — affected: ingest-gpu-pool-3
Jordan: Trace ID: `trace-0a1b2c3d` — found a few `ws_send` spans with long tail times, and an upstream throttling event in the same trace. Posting the jaeger link: https://jaeger.redwood.company/trace/trace-0a1b2c3d
Irene: Thanks — that trace looks like client-side slow reads causing backlog on the server write buffers, which can produce partial frames when we flush smaller chunks. Two things to check: i) which client version (old clients had smaller write windows), ii) whether the pool hit transient GPU contention — check `node.metrics.gpu_utilization` around the same window.
Alex: For the alert tuning, here's a quick patch suggestion you can drop into the rules file: ```yaml
- alert: PartialFrameRateHigh
  expr: rate(streaming_ws_partial_frame_total[2m]) / rate(streaming_ws_frames_total[2m]) > 0.08
  for: 1m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "High partial frame rate on ingest"
```
Sam: If we change it, let's run the new rule in `warning` first and monitor for 48h before promoting to page.
Lee: Also useful to add a dashboard panel for `ws_send.queue_depth` per node — that surfaced a backlog during the last incident.
Jordan: Great pointers. I'll file a tiny follow-up: 1) open PR for alert change as `warning` with 48h monitor; 2) add `ws_send.queue_depth` panel to the live-ingest dashboard; 3) follow up on client version if we see repeated tail latency. Will ping for CR. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Alex: ping me on the PR for a quick review.
Sam: I'll schedule the 48h watch and post a note in #incidents if the rate stays elevated.
Irene: If it reappears after tuning, we should consider a short canary that forces smaller chunk sizes to see if behavior improves.
Jordan: Copy. I'll start with the alert PR and dashboard patch.
